First, we rewrite the given inequality so that the right-hand side equals zero. Then, we factor the left-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+16x+20 & <3x-22 \\ {x}^{2}+13x+42 & <0 \\ (x+7)(x+6) & <0\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the roots of the corresponding equation $(x+7)(x+6)=0.$ The roots are $x=-7$ and $x=-6,$ and they split the number line into the $3$ subintervals $(-\infty ,-7),$ $(-7,-6),$ and $(-6,\infty ).$

Now, we construct a sign table with the list of the intervals on the top and the list of factors on the left. Filling in the sign table using the usual method, we get the following result:

|  | $(-\infty ,-7)$ | $(-7,-6)$ | $(-6,\infty )$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $x+7$ | $-$ | $+$ | $+$ |
| $x+6$ | $-$ | $-$ | $+$ |
| $(x+7)(x+6)$ | $+$ | $-$ | $+$ |

Finally, to solve the quadratic inequality $(x+7)(x+6)<0,$ we look at the bottom row to find out where the expression $(x+7)(x+6)$ is negative.

We see that the expression is negative on the interval $(-7,-6).$

Therefore, we conclude that ${x}^{2}+16x+20<3x-22$ for all 

$$
x\in (-7,-6).
$$
